issues.t: IVT check engine light with transmission codes
issues.sym: Check engine light comes on; the transmission may feel off or slip. Stored codes point to gear ratio, pulley pressure or transmission control problems (such as P0730, P0741 or P1603).
issues.why: Hyundai found some 2020-2022 Venues with the IVT (Hyundai's CVT automatic) set these codes. The first fix is new transmission control software; some cars needed the IVT itself replaced.
issues.next: Have a Hyundai dealer read the codes and check for bulletin 23-01-019H. The transmission is covered by Hyundai's powertrain warranty for the original owner, so go to a dealer first.

issues.t: IVT check engine light from oil pressure sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with transmission codes, usually without any change in how the car drives.
issues.why: A faulty oil pressure sensor on the IVT can report bad readings and set codes. Hyundai's bulletin says to replace the sensor rather than the whole transmission.
issues.next: Have the codes read at a Hyundai dealer and ask about bulletin 23-AT-010H. It is a small part and is usually a quick repair.

issues.t: Front seat belt pretensioner can burst (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving. The risk is in a crash, when the front seat belt pretensioner fires.
issues.why: The pretensioner tightens the belt in a crash. On these Venues it could burst when it fired and throw metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.next: Check your VIN on Hyundai's recall site or NHTSA. Dealers fit a cap over the pretensioner (or replaced it on some 2021 cars) for free.

issues.t: EGR valve short can cut engine power (recall)
issues.sym: Check engine light and a sudden loss of drive power while driving.
issues.why: An electrical short inside the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve can shut down engine power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-308. Dealers replace the EGR valve for free. If power drops, steer to a safe spot and turn on the hazards.

issues.sym: The horn is silent or works only now and then. Some 2024 owners report the horn going out within the first 15,000 miles.
issues.why: Hyundai found that foreign material can get inside the horn on 2020-2022 Venues and corrode its internal parts.
issues.next: A working horn is a safety item. Have a dealer check it under bulletin 23-BE-009H; a new horn is usually covered while the car is under warranty.

issues.t: Key-start Venues are easy to steal
issues.sym: The car is stolen or the steering column and ignition are found broken open.
issues.why: Key-start Venues of these years were built without an engine immobilizer, so thieves can start them with a simple tool. Hyundai added an anti-theft software update and a steering wheel lock program.
issues.next: Get the free anti-theft software update (campaign 993) at a Hyundai dealer and put on the window sticker. A steering wheel lock adds more protection.

issues.sym: The engine shuts off without warning while driving or at a stop, sometimes with warning lights.
issues.why: Owners of 2020 Venues report random stalling; no single cause has been confirmed, so a dealer needs to check stored codes and any software updates.
issues.next: Note when it happens and any warning messages, and take it to a Hyundai dealer while it is under warranty. If it stalls while moving, get off the road safely.

issues.t: Moisture or fog inside headlights or taillights
issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside the headlights, taillights or fog lights, especially after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Moisture can build up inside the lamp housings. Hyundai issued bulletins on how to tell normal light condensation from a real leak.
issues.next: Light fog that clears after driving with the lights on is usually normal. Water pooling or a burned-out bulb means the lamp is leaking and should be replaced under warranty.

issues.t: Apple CarPlay or Android Auto drops out
issues.sym: Wireless CarPlay disconnects by itself, or phone projection won't connect or keeps dropping.
issues.why: Software problems in the head unit and USB connection issues. Hyundai released bulletins and head-unit software updates for these symptoms.
issues.next: Try a different, good-quality USB cable and update your phone. Then ask a dealer to load the latest head-unit software, or install it yourself from Hyundai's update site.

issues.t: Radio app crashes or false 'Uneven road ahead' message
issues.sym: The radio app on the touch screen keeps crashing, or the dash shows an 'Uneven road ahead' warning when the road is fine.
issues.why: A software bug in the navigation head unit. Hyundai issued a software update for it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the update in bulletin 24-BE-001H. It is a software fix and does not affect how the car drives.

issues.t: Screen or instrument display goes black
issues.sym: The center touch screen goes black now and then, or the instrument display goes blank so you can't see speed or fuel level.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a software update for key-start Venues whose audio screen could go black. Owners of 2024 models also report the gauge display going blank, which a battery disconnect only fixed for a while.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for software updates (bulletin 24-BE-004H for the screen). A blank speedometer is a safety concern, so report it to the dealer right away.

issues.t: Driver attention warning beeps too often
issues.sym: A coffee-cup warning and loud chime keep going off on the highway, even when you're alert or just checking mirrors.
issues.why: The driver attention warning system watches steering patterns and can be overly sensitive. Owners report it can't be fully turned off.
issues.next: Check the settings menu for sensitivity options. If it's alerting constantly, tell the dealer and ask about updates.

issues.sym: The oil service reminder stays on the dash after an oil change, and the touch screen won't clear it.
issues.why: A software problem between the gauge cluster and the head unit. Hyundai issued a bulletin with the fix.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletin 23-01-078H. It's not a mechanical problem; just make sure the oil was actually changed.

issues.sym: The rear hatch doesn't latch unless you slam it.
issues.why: The rubber bumpers that stop the tailgate can be set wrong. Hyundai issued a bulletin to adjust them.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to adjust the tailgate bumpers under bulletin 20-BD-011H. It's a quick adjustment.

issues.t: Door lock settings won't stay set
issues.sym: Automatic door lock or unlock settings you chose don't stick, or the doors lock and unlock differently than set.
issues.why: Owners report the personal settings for door locks on early Venues not working as expected; this points to a body control software issue.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the body control module for software updates.
